governance.disclaimer: Recommendations are psychoeducational tools for reflective growth, not medical or psychiatric treatment.

body.why: Grounding disrupts sympathetic nervous system overdrive by engaging external somatic senses, pulling focus away from racing catastrophic thoughts.
body.what: A structured sensory enumeration exercise performed in 3 to 5 minutes.
how: Scan your environment and name 5 distinct things you can see.
Touch and consciously acknowledge 4 physical textures (e.g. your desk, sleeve, watch).
Identify 3 distinct ambient sounds (e.g. clock ticking, distant traffic).
Notice 2 things you can smell or scents nearby.
Acknowledge 1 positive taste, sensation, or something you are currently grateful for.
body.measure: Check subjective anxiety intensity (0-10) before and 10 minutes following the exercise.
body.professional_support_when: If panic attacks occur regularly or anxiety impairs daily responsibilities for multiple consecutive weeks.

body.why: Regulated equal-ratio breathing balances sympathetic and parasympathetic branches of the autonomic nervous system, decelerating heart rate.
body.what: A portable physiological reset technique used in high-stress operational environments.
how: Exhale completely through your mouth.
Inhale smoothly through your nose for 4 counts.
Gently hold your breath with full lungs for 4 counts.
Exhale steadily through your mouth for 4 counts.
Hold your breath empty for 4 counts.
Repeat the cycle 4 to 6 times.
body.measure: Notice deceleration in breathing rate and relaxation in shoulder/jaw tension.
body.professional_support_when: When chronic stress leads to persistent insomnia, gastrointestinal distress, or feelings of complete burnout.

body.why: Immediate anger surges narrow cognitive appraisals into hostility; an intentional delay restores prefrontal executive evaluation.
body.what: A 90-second physiological pause coupled with three reframing questions before communicating.
how: Step away physically or declare a 90-second pause before replying to a provoking message.
Ask: 'What is another plausible, non-hostile interpretation of the other person's intention?'
Ask: 'Will my desired response advance my long-term relationship or goal?'
State your boundary or grievance using 'I' statements rather than accusatory 'You' statements.
body.measure: Fewer instances of regrettable reactive speech or impulsive escalation.
body.professional_support_when: If anger escalates into physical intimidation, property damage, or severe interpersonal rupture.

rules.title: Micro Behavioral Activation & Self-Compassion
citations: Martell et al. (2010) Behavioral Activation for Depression

body.why: Sadness drives social withdrawal and physical immobility, which inadvertently intensifies low mood. Small deliberate actions rebuild momentum.
body.what: A low-demand, manageable activity scheduled without requiring initial motivation.
how: Select one small 10-minute task (e.g. a walk in daylight, making tea, tidying one counter).
Acknowledge the sadness kindly: 'It makes sense that I feel down right now.'
Perform the small task gently, focusing attention on sensory steps rather than outcome.
Avoid demanding high energy or joyful feelings from yourself during the task.
body.measure: Record whether completing the micro-step yielded a small sense of dignity or relief.
body.professional_support_when: If feelings of persistent sadness or anhedonia persist continuously for more than two weeks.

body.why: Strong outcome drive and assertiveness can inadvertently intimidate collaborators and miss valuable bottom-up insights.
body.what: A conversational checkpoint practice that prioritizes inquiry before instruction.
how: In team discussions, deliberately allow three other people to speak before offering your directive.
Ask at least two open-ended questions: 'What risks am I missing?' or 'How would you approach this?'
Summarize another person's proposal before evaluating it.
body.measure: Increased team engagement and fewer misunderstandings in group projects.
body.professional_support_when: If aggressive impatience damages critical professional partnerships.

body.why: Exacting quality standards provide excellence but can trap high-melancholic thinkers in analysis paralysis and chronic rumination.
body.what: A pre-commitment rule establishing when a task has reached practical completeness.
how: Define 'objective completeness' criteria before beginning a detailed analysis or project.
Set a hard time boundary for editing and review passes (maximum 2 review cycles).
Ship or submit work when it satisfies the predetermined standard, accepting imperfect aesthetics.
body.measure: Reduction in project turnaround time and reduced end-of-day mental fatigue.
body.professional_support_when: When perfectionistic standards cause debilitating procrastination or severe burnout.

body.why: A preference for relational peace can lead to habitual compliance, masking valuable personal needs and creative ideas.
body.what: A structured practice to state preferences clearly without requiring conflict.
how: Identify one decision each week where you would normally default to 'whatever everyone wants'.
Express your genuine preference early in the discussion.
Practice comfortable ownership of boundaries: 'I am unable to take that on right now, but I can support on X.'
body.measure: Noticeable reduction in unspoken resentment and greater personal agency.
body.professional_support_when: When conflict avoidance leads to tolerating unhealthy boundaries.

body.why: High enthusiasm generates excellent initial momentum, but novelty fatigue can cause follow-through drop-offs on details.
body.what: Implementation intentions linking high energy moments to structured execution commitments.
how: Pair every new exciting commitment with a written calendar slot immediately.
Use the 'Rule of Two': Only take on a new initiative once two existing projects are finalized.
Engage an accountability buddy or shared dashboard to report completion milestones.
body.measure: Higher completion percentage for initiated personal and professional projects.
body.professional_support_when: If overcommitment leads to chronic unreliability or severe life disruption.
